Præco edicito, cui videtur N. in-iustè fecisse perforatum calculum mittito: integrum vero, cui non videtur iniustè fecisse.
Paribus calculis secundum reum pronuntiato.
Cados apponunto pro litigantium numero.

Siquis coierit, aut data vel accepta pecunia corruperit Heliæam, aut quoduis aliud Atheniensium forum, aut Senatum, aut cœtum fecerit ad evertendam Rempublicam, aut advocatus pecuniam accipiat litis causa, sive privatæ, sive publicæ: Eorum nomina apud Thesmothetas cuiuis deferre ius esto.

Intra quinquennium læsi dicam scribunto.
Exceptione utitor, si in ius vocetur ad Magistratum, cuius ea non est iu-risdictio.
In ius vocatus apud Magistratum Atheniensium propter contractus, [illegible, ~20 letters]qui neq. omnino Athenis facti sunt, neque aliunde mercis Athenas importare cauent, exceptione fori utitor.

page.notes: Greek text is read from a small, blurred scan; many Greek words, accents and breathings are uncertain and should be checked against the original. Doubtful Greek readings were not marked individually except where noted. The Latin line "rentionem condemnationémve dedu" is set in the same column and is copied as printed, with the first letters cut. The subtitle "Seruus homo causam ne orato." is uncertain in its first word. Superscript marks after εἶ) and similar forms appear as small signs above the line and are copied as best read. Paragraph breaks follow the indents in the column. The right half of the scan is blank. The Greek marginal note at the left is too faint to read letter by letter and is marked illegible. Doubtful readings: "pacisćitor" (the printed form has a diacritic on the c, unclear), "in-ictum" (the line break hides the start of the word), and "iu-risdictio" (the spelling of the hyphenated word is kept as printed). The "d" below the last line is taken as a catchword-like mark.
